key_insight: The paper shows that robotic policies often fail at compositional generalization because they rely on biased shortcuts tied to specific instruction factors like color, verb, object, size, and spatial terms. It proposes a bias-aware framework to diagnose these failures and guide better data collection for more robust language grounding.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of robots following novel, multi-part instructions reliably instead of overfitting to superficial cues in the training data.
method: Defines "instruction factor bias" to measure how strongly a policy over-relies on individual semantic components of an instruction.
Introduces a diagnostic evaluation framework that isolates failures by instruction factor, helping pinpoint which language concepts are poorly grounded.
Uses bias-aware analysis to inform strategic data collection and scaling, improving compositional generalization in robotic manipulation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper provides a practical way to debug and improve instruction-following policies beyond aggregate success rates. It helps teams collect the right data, identify hidden shortcut learning, and build robots that generalize to new combinations of known concepts.

paper_title: Scale Up Strategically: Learning Compositional Generalization via Bias-Aware Evaluation and Data Collection for Robotic Manipulation
paper_authors: Yu Qi, Zhang Ye, Xinyi Xu, Yuxuan Lu, Amitoj Sandhu
